summary.name: How to get started with site reliability engineering (SRE)
summary.one_liner: An O'Reilly interview with Google SRE Stephen Thorne on how organizations of any size can start and run an SRE practice.
keywords: automate yourself out of a job
use_cases: Starting an SRE team at a small or mid-sized company
Getting management buy-in for reliability work
Measuring whether an SRE team is delivering impact
summary.what_it_does: This is an article based on an interview with Google site reliability engineer Stephen Thorne, co-author of The Site Reliability Workbook. It covers how to get management buy-in for SRE by framing it as a way to address reliability, operational load, and costs. It discusses psychological safety as a barrier, and why postmortems should be blameless so that other causes of failure keep being investigated. It also describes what a successful SRE team looks like: it knows its system's reliability, has a plan to improve it, and can show measurable impact.
notable: Interview with a Google SRE, co-author of The Site Reliability Workbook
Focuses on applying SRE at small as well as large organizations
Covers blameless postmortems and psychological safety in production teams
caveats: Discusses general principles only; no concrete tooling or step-by-step setup guide is shown in the text
